lesson.grammar_point: present perfect with for and since and how long

listenings.text: Hi, it's Tom again, the recruiter from Miami. I have worked as a recruiter for twelve years, and I have read thousands of profiles. Here is my secret: I read three things first. First, the headline. Second, the first two lines of the summary. Third, the dates: how long has this person worked in the area, and how long have they been in the current job? I love numbers. When a person writes: I have led a team of fifteen people since 2020, I understand the experience in two seconds. And one more thing: if your profile is in English, I can send it to my clients in other countries. That is a big advantage.

Hello, I'm Rachel, and this is the summary on my profile. I have worked in human resources for twenty years. I started in payroll, and I have been an HR director since 2018. I am based in Edinburgh, but I have led teams in Scotland, Ireland and Sweden. I have a degree in psychology. My biggest achievement? We have reduced the time to hire a new person from sixty days to thirty. I love training new managers, and I have mentored more than forty people. I am always happy to connect with people in my network, so please send me a message.

reading.rtitle: How to Write a Profile Recruiters Read
paras: Recruiters look at hundreds of profiles every week, and they decide fast: often in less than ten seconds. So the first lines are the most important. Start with a clear headline: not only your job title, but what you do. “Head of HR” is fine; “Head of HR · people, culture and growth” is better.

Then write a short summary, in the first person. Say how long you have worked in your area, what you have led and one or two achievements with numbers. For example: “I have worked in human resources for eighteen years, and I have been the Head of HR at a logistics company since 2019. I have led a team of twelve people, and I have reduced turnover by thirty percent.”

Finally, keep your profile active. Add your degree and your languages, say where you are based, and connect with people in your network. Many professionals have never updated their profile since their last job. Recruiters notice that. A profile in English also says something important: I am ready for international opportunities.
